rationale:
ROUND 6 of 7ba5b8c4. Round 5 was the first COMPLETE council since round 1 (unreadable:0 -- editquality parsed after being absent for three rounds) and it immediately raised the FIRST HIGH-SEVERITY objection of the whole sequence. Its absence was costing real review.

THE HEADLINE: ROUND 5'S 'DURABLE SURFACE' FIX COULD NOT HAVE WORKED, AND THE COUNCIL PROVED IT.
editquality (HIGH): the site_work_items INSERT -- the fix for the blocking objection -- was written as a COMMENT in the sketch, not as code: 'a described intention that may not land in the shipped code'. debug_historian (medium) went further and asked whether the row could land at all, since site_work_items looks per-site while this is a repo-wide indexer. CHECKED:
  SELECT column_name, is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='site_work_items';
  -> site_id NO | handler_agent NO | pipeline NO | item_type NO | status NO | item_key YES
**site_id, handler_agent and pipeline are all NOT NULL.** The code indexer has no site, no handler agent and no pipeline in that sense. The INSERT would have FAILED, so round 5's headline fix was not merely pseudocode -- it was pseudocode for something impossible. I asserted a durable surface I had not checked the shape of, one round after being told that logging-only was insufficient.

SO THE SURFACE CHANGES TO doc_notes, WHICH IS REUSE RATHER THAN INVENTION. This subsystem ALREADY keeps its trail there: migration 244 created doc_notes rows under subject_key='index_code_symbols' and 'diagnose_code_lookup' (4 rows, defect-then-fix per action). doc_notes.site_id is NULLABLE; subject_type accepts 'action'. It is append-only with NO dedup index, which also answers guidelines (medium): the idx_swi_dedup contract (UNIQUE(site_id,item_key) over non-terminal statuses, DELETE+INSERT not ON CONFLICT) governs site_work_items and does not apply here -- a repeating refusal appends to a log, which is what a log is for, rather than flooding a triage queue.

guardian (medium) asked who CONSUMES a brand-new item_type, warning that an unclaimed row 'just sits inert for ever -- the same no-reader failure mode this round is trying to fix for logs, reintroduced one layer up'. That is exactly right, and the honest answer is the one it offered as acceptable: **there is NO automated consumer, and I am not inventing one.** doc_notes is read by whoever investigates this subsystem -- the travelling-docs trail this workstream already maintains and cites. Claiming a triage lifecycle I have not wired would repeat the error above.

reuse_agent (medium) asked whether a helper already exists for creating work items from an action. FOUND: `create_work_item` is a registered ACTION (registry.go:619, create_work_item_action.go:82). It is a workflow STEP, not a callable helper, and it writes the same site-scoped table -- so it does not fit a repo-wide indexer either. Recorded as searched-and-does-not-fit, with the reason. reuse_agent (low) asked about an existing destructive-delete ratio guard to extend: searched, none exists.

guardian (low) -- blast radius of the zero-match-glob HARD ERROR. Right: a bad glob would have taken down CODE indexing too, where before it merely under-counted. NARROWED: a zero-match glob now fails the DOC half only. Code rows still upsert and prune normally; doc rows are skipped and NOT pruned; the refusal is recorded in doc_notes and the result payload. Loud, durable, proportionate.

debug_historian (low) -- where prune_floor_ratio is read from, since 'set it to 0 for one run' is unachievable if it is static agent config. It is read from the STEP config via datahelpers (GetFloatField(config, 'prune_floor_ratio', 0.5)), the same mechanism as every other tunable in this action, so a one-off dispatch can override it without editing agent_definitions.

prior_art_librarian (low) -- the 'no reader switches on kind' claim had been carried by memory for five rounds. Re-checked THIS round rather than restated, and it did NOT come back clean: `grep -rnE 'kind\s*==\s*"(func|method|struct)"|case "(func|method|struct)":'` returned ONE hit, scripts/documentation_project/02/assembler.go:347. Resolved: it switches on the ANALYSER's typeDef.Kind, and `grep -n code_symbols` on that file returns nothing -- it never touches the table. The claim survives, but it took a check to establish, which was the objection's whole point.

editquality (low) -- VERIFY #4 still needs a human to run the shell pipeline and eyeball the diff. Conceded: edit 6 is self-declared a supplement that covers no mechanism. It now emits per-path counts so the comparison is legible, but it is not mechanised, and it is not claimed to be.

plan.summary: ROUND 6. D11 layer 1b: index MARKDOWN sections into code_symbols. Round 6 replaces round 5's site_work_items surface -- which was pseudocode for an IMPOSSIBLE row (site_id/handler_agent/pipeline are NOT NULL; this indexer is repo-wide) -- with a doc_notes entry written as real code, reusing the trail this subsystem already keeps. A zero-match glob now fails the doc half only, leaving code indexing intact.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian (round 1, medium): no reader switches on kind; diagnose_code_lookup never selects it; scanCodeSymbolRows selects it into lookup_code_symbols' result map only. NUMBER MOVES -- 253 is highest today, but this workstream's last migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours. Re-read the max immediately before writing the file.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

ROUND 3, rewritten for bug_historian (medium): the round-2 guard fired only on a TOTAL of zero, and round 1's real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source. Now: counts are tracked PER GLOB and returned; a glob matching ZERO FILES is a hard error (the plan's only fail-loud escalation, because a source contributing nothing is indistinguishable from a source that does not exist); and the scope/path-shape assertion runs HERE, every index, not only in a VERIFY a human runs once. NOT REUSING, with the search attached in the rationale: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection (vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650) is markdown- and heading-aware but TRUNCATES at a fixed end-marker list and returns one prefix with no spans; no markdown parser is a dependency (goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere). Suffix determinism, for guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence gets the same suffix every run -- document order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

ROUND 6: the durable surface is doc_notes, as REAL CODE. Round 5's site_work_items INSERT was a comment (editquality HIGH) for a row that could not exist (debug_historian medium): site_id, handler_agent and pipeline are all NOT NULL and this indexer is repo-wide. doc_notes is where this subsystem's trail already lives (migration 244), its site_id is nullable, it is append-only so the idx_swi_dedup contract does not apply (guidelines), and it has NO automated consumer -- stated plainly rather than invented (guardian). A zero-match glob now fails the DOC half only, so code indexing is unaffected (guardian low). prune_floor_ratio comes from step config via datahelpers, so a one-off dispatch can override it (debug_historian low).

A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT, unchanged: content and content_hash must not gain section text, or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST IS REAL AND NEW: ~1,749 rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this one is not, and it is stated rather than buried. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: measured at 1 today. The suffix counter runs in document order over a single top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs -- if a reviewer can show a path where it is not, the prune/upsert churns those rows every index. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE ALREADY: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries. That is the failure mode in miniature -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with exactly the stale-doc class the plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. The VERIFY's out-of-scope assertion and the register_sections check are the guards, and the Go comment marks the value load-bearing. (5) BLAST RADIUS OF THE CHECK CHANGE, now enumerated rather than assumed: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k. (6) ROLLBACK ORDER: the old CHECK is validated against existing data, so kind='doc' rows must be deleted BEFORE the constraint is restored -- the sidecar does both in one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls, so the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break. Confirm against the RUNNING pod with a string this change creates plus one it deletes, never git and never the tag. (8) The freshness banner keys on the indexed COMMIT (108 defect A, live v1.0.1189), so a prose answer carries the same staleness qualifier a code answer does.
